AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing student and early-career web developer with hands-on experience building React interfaces and accessible web features. Project experience spans TypeScript, Node.js/Express APIs, PostgreSQL, and automated testing. Developed an accessibility-focused final-year project tested with screen readers and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication
Testing and accessibility: Jest, React Testing Library, screen-reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver), Storybook
Other: Chart.js, Vercel

EXPERIENCE
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media
May 2024 – Aug 2024
- Worked on accessibility fixes and React components for a news website.
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages.
- Documented the gallery component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab
Spring 2025 | One semester
- Supported approximately 30 students during first-year web development lab sessions.

PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app for sea swimmers showing tides, water temperature, and weather around the Irish coast.
- Developed the frontend with React and TypeScript, and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs.
- Used PostgreSQL to store user favourites and Chart.js to present data.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Awarded 82% (First Class); demonstrated at the college project showcase.

Yoga Studio Booking Site | Freelance | 2025
- Built marketing pages and a class timetable with booking requests sent by email.
- Used Next.js static generation and Tailwind CSS; deployed on Vercel.
- Set up content editing through Markdown files.

Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon | 2024
- Collaborated in a three-person team to build a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; placed second.
- Developed the frontend.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a four-person student project: a web app matching classmates for study sessions.
- Used JavaScript and Firebase Authentication; other team members developed the API and database.

VOLUNTEERING
Social Media Volunteer | Sea Swimming Club
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

EDUCATION
Computing | Liffey Institute of Technology
Third-year student

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, and professionally oriented toward junior web development. It presents strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, testing, and Storybook through projects and internship experience. The Tidewatch project is especially persuasive because it includes a measurable Lighthouse score and academic result. However, the CV is not submission-ready because the contact details remain placeholders. It also does not clearly distinguish professional experience from academic/project experience, which matters for a role requiring 2+ years of professional experience. Some bullets could communicate scope and contribution more precisely, but the document generally avoids unsupported claims.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The standard section headings, chronological experience structure, plain-text technology names, and keyword coverage should parse well in most ATS platforms. Strong searchable terms include React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Jest, React Testing Library, accessibility, screen-reader testing, Storybook, and Firebase Authentication. AI screening probability is moderate: the CV will likely match strongly for React/TypeScript, Node.js/SQL project experience, accessibility, Next.js, and Storybook, but ranking may be reduced because it does not explicitly show Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, English proficiency, or 2+ years of professional experience. The contact placeholders are also a significant professionalism and parsing problem. Do not add unsupported tools such as Git, Playwright, Docker, AWS, or OWASP experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: This is a credible junior-level match with particularly strong alignment to Verdane Care's accessibility and patient-focused product context. The candidate demonstrates React and TypeScript, Node.js/Express APIs, PostgreSQL, automated unit/component testing, screen-reader testing, Next.js, wellness-related work through the yoga studio site, and Storybook. Tidewatch also demonstrates work on a user-facing data application and responsible attention to accessibility. The main objective gap is the requirement for 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript web-application experience: the documented internship lasted approximately four months, while the remaining experience is academic, freelance, hackathon, or personal/project work. The CV also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP/security awareness, health-data privacy, German/Croatian, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B testing. These are candidate-experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than defects that can be solved by adding keywords. The wellness project and accessibility background provide the closest truthful connection to Verdane Care's healthcare and user-centered environment.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL
1. In the contact header, replace "[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO]" with the candidate's actual professional email address, phone number, and working LinkedIn or portfolio URL. Remove all square-bracket placeholders before submission.

2. In the Experience section, revise the Harbourline Media entry so its professional scope is unmistakable without overstating it. For example, change "Worked on accessibility fixes and React components for a news website" to "Contributed to accessibility fixes and React components for a news website during a four-month software development internship." Keep the existing gallery, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library bullets because they are supported by the original candidate material.

3. In the Professional Summary section, make the level of experience explicit so the CV does not imply that academic projects are equivalent to two years of professional experience. For example, change the opening to: "Third-year Computing student and early-career web developer with a software development internship and hands-on project experience building React and TypeScript interfaces..."

HIGH-VALUE ATS/ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS
4. Add a short "Additional Information" or "Languages" line near the end of the CV stating "English: Fluent". This is supported by the candidate's original English-language application material. Do not add German or Croatian because they are not supported by the original candidate information.

5. In the Tidewatch project entry, make the backend and testing keywords more ATS-readable while preserving the truthful project context. For example, change the relevant bullets to: "Built a Node.js/Express backend API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs" and "Used Jest for automated testing and tested the interface with NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers." Do not describe the testing as end-to-end testing because that is not supported.

6. In the Technical Skills section, change "Testing and accessibility: Jest, React Testing Library, screen-reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver), Storybook" to "Testing: Jest, React Testing Library | Accessibility: screen-reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver), Lighthouse, Storybook" if the candidate wants Lighthouse to be searchable as a distinct skill. Keep the Lighthouse score and result in the Tidewatch project as evidence rather than presenting it as a certification.

MINOR PRESENTATION IMPROVEMENTS
7. In the Teaching Assistant entry, change "Supported approximately 30 students during first-year web development lab sessions" to "Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of first-year web development lab sessions." This uses the fuller timing and scope already present in the candidate information.

8. In the Yoga Studio Booking Site project, retain the term "freelance" but make the wellness relevance clearer by changing the heading to "Yoga Studio Booking Site | Freelance wellness project | 2025". This is supported by the original project information and provides a truthful connection to the employer's wellness and healthcare domain.

9. Add dates to the Social Media Volunteer entry if they are known; otherwise leave the entry without invented dates. If no additional responsibilities are available, keep the current single bullet rather than expanding it with unsupported claims.
critique.critical_issues: The CV is not submission-ready because the header still contains the literal placeholders "[EMAIL]", "[PHONE]", and "[LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO]". These must be replaced with real contact details. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected when cross-referenced against the Original Candidate Information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, readable, and professionally targeted toward a junior React/TypeScript or full-stack position. It presents strong evidence of accessibility work, React/TypeScript projects, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, testing, Next.js, and Storybook. The project bullets are more specific and credible than generic student-CV statements, especially the Tidewatch results: an 82% First Class grade, screen-reader testing, and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The main content limitation is that the document can appear stronger than the candidate's professional experience actually is: nearly all full-stack/backend experience is academic or project-based, while the internship lasted four months and the advertised role requests at least two years of professional experience. The CV generally handles this honestly, but the distinction should remain clear. The Teaching Assistant and hackathon experience are relevant and useful, although the Teaching Assistant entry could show more concrete technical or mentoring responsibilities if supported by the candidate's information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, chronological dates, simple bullet points, and searchable technology names such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, Storybook, and Vercel. It should parse reliably. Screening probability is medium-high for junior React/frontend searches and medium for this particular full-stack role because several exact requirements are absent or only partially represented: semantic HTML, responsive layouts, Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, OWASP Top 10, and health-data privacy. Do not add these keywords unless supported by the candidate's actual experience. The combined skills line using a vertical bar is still generally parseable, but separate labeled lines or bullets would be slightly safer for ATS extraction.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with React and TypeScript, accessible patient-facing interfaces, Node.js/Express APIs, PostgreSQL, automated unit/component testing, Next.js, wellness-related work, and Storybook. Tidewatch is particularly relevant to a patient-experience product because it demonstrates an accessible data-driven web application, third-party API integration, user favourites, and screen-reader testing. The Yoga Studio project provides a relevant wellness-sector connection. The candidate does not meet the stated 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience: the material shows a four-month internship plus academic, freelance, and personal projects. The document also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP/security awareness, GDPR or health-data privacy experience, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, or analytics/A-B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps or unverified areas rather than defects that can be solved by wording. The CV aligns well with the company's accessibility, user-focused, and wellness-adjacent interests, but it is a stretch match for the advertised level and must be evaluated as an early-career application.

If the candidate actually provided code guidance, debugging help, or explanations of web-development concepts, those verified activities should be added because they strengthen the mentoring alignment; do not add them without confirmation.

4. In the Technical Skills section, consider separating each category onto its own clearly labeled line or bullet instead of combining "Jest, React Testing Library | Accessibility..." on one line. Use labels such as "Frontend," "Backend and Databases," "Testing," "Accessibility," and "Other." This preserves all current keywords while improving ATS extraction and human scanning.

5. In the Projects section under Tidewatch, retain the existing backend and testing evidence but make the end-to-end scope clearer without overstating it. It presents relevant technical projects effectively, especially Tidewatch, the accessible gallery component, and the wellness booking site. The strongest evidence is specific and credible: React/TypeScript development, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, screen-reader testing, Storybook, and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The main content limitation is that the education entry is very brief and the header does not include contact or portfolio details. critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience formatting, plain text bullets, and recognizable technology names. Keyword coverage is strong for React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Jest, React Testing Library, accessibility, Storybook, and Vercel. AI screening probability is moderate to high for a junior React/full-stack role, but likely lower for this specific vacancy if the screening system strictly applies the 2+ years of professional experience requirement. Terms that are not supported by the candidate material should not be added: Git workflows, end-to-end testing, Playwright, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP Top 10, GDPR/health-data privacy, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B testing. Tidewatch is particularly relevant because it demonstrates an end-to-end application with a user-facing interface, backend API, SQL data storage, testing, and accessibility evaluation. The candidate's material shows a gap against the must-have requirement for 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript web-application experience: the documented professional internship lasted four months, while the remaining experience is academic, freelance, or hackathon work. The material also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive-layout knowledge, OWASP/security awareness, or health-data privacy experience. Nice-to-have alignment is good for Next.js, wellness-related work, and Storybook; German/Croatian, AWS/Docker, and analytics/A/B testing are not supported by the candidate material.
